channel.title: Web Standards Weekly
channel.description: Tracking W3C, IETF, WHATWG, and TC39 activity.

item.title: CSS Anchor Positioning Reaches Candidate Recommendation
item.description: The W3C CSS Working Group published CSS Anchor Positioning as a Candidate Recommendation, formalising the anchor-name and position-anchor properties that allow elements to be positioned relative to arbitrary anchors elsewhere in the document.

item.title: TC39 Advances Signals Proposal to Stage 3
item.description: TC39 advanced the Signals proposal to stage 3, introducing a first-class reactive primitive to JavaScript that harmonises with framework-level reactivity systems already in widespread use.

item.title: WHATWG Merges Invoker Commands into the HTML Living Standard
item.description: WHATWG merged the Invoker Commands spec into the HTML Living Standard, adding the invoketarget and invokeaction attributes to button and input elements for declarative UI interactions.

item.title: IETF RFC 9728: HTTP Resumable Uploads Published
item.description: IETF published RFC 9728, defining a standard protocol for resumable HTTP uploads that allows clients to resume interrupted transfers from the last acknowledged byte rather than restarting from the beginning.

item.title: WebAssembly Garbage Collection Reaches Phase 4
item.description: The WebAssembly Working Group announced that the Garbage Collection extension reached Phase 4, completing the standardisation process and enabling managed-memory languages like Kotlin and Dart to compile to Wasm without bundling a custom GC.

item.title: CSS Color Level 5 Functions Land in Safari 20
item.description: Safari 20 shipped support for CSS Color Level 5 functions including color-mix() with all interpolation methods and relative color syntax, bringing full cross-browser parity for the new color features.
